issues.t: Rod knock and sudden engine failure
issues.sym: A ticking that turns into a deep knock from the engine, often after months of using oil, then the engine locks up or a connecting rod breaks through the block. Reports cluster around 63,000-135,000 miles.
issues.why: Engines that burn oil run low between changes. Starved of oil, the rod bearings wear and spin until the engine fails. Owners commonly end up replacing the engine.
issues.next: If you hear knocking, check the oil right away and stop driving if it's low. A knock usually means the bearings are already damaged, so get quotes on a used or rebuilt engine rather than a quick fix.

issues.t: Heavy oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops fast, as much as a quart every 500 miles, with blue-gray exhaust smoke, a low-oil light or misfire codes. Owners often find the dipstick dry.
issues.why: The piston oil-control rings on this engine family can stick or clog with carbon, letting oil into the cylinders to burn. The same 1.8L engine has the same reputation in the Corolla of these years.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and top it off. Ask a shop about a ring-cleaning treatment; if it is burning a lot, budget for rings or a replacement engine before it knocks.

issues.t: Engine failure on early GT-S models
issues.sym: A check engine light, then engine noise, and finally the engine quitting, around 65,000-72,000 miles. Some owners had it happen twice.
issues.why: The high-revving GT-S engine is hard on its valvetrain and oil. Owners blame a design weakness in early cars; worn lift bolts (see the separate issue) and low oil are known contributors, but no single cause was confirmed.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time, and have the lift bolts checked. If the engine is knocking or down on power, get a diagnosis before more damage is done.

issues.t: Worn or broken valve lift bolts
issues.sym: A ticking or clacking from the top of the engine, especially when the high-rpm cam ('lift') kicks in, or the lift no longer engaging.
issues.why: Two small bolts hold the rocker arm shafts that run the GT-S's high-rpm cam lobes. The original bolts wear heavily and can snap. Toyota bulletin EG010-03 introduced a redesigned, tapered bolt.
issues.next: Have the original-style bolts replaced with the newer part. It is a cheap, quick job that can prevent much bigger engine damage.

issues.t: Power loss or no lift above 6,000 rpm
issues.sym: The engine feels flat or stumbles at high revs under hard acceleration, or the expected surge when the lift engages comes and goes.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin 01003 covers intermittent power loss or uneven variable valve lift above 6,000 rpm under high load. Low oil or worn lift parts make it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. Ask a Toyota dealer or Celica specialist to check the lift system and apply the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Engine oil sludge (oil gelling)
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers, the engine runs rough or loses power, oil looks thick or tarry, and in bad cases the engine seizes.
issues.why: On 2.2L Celicas built from August 1996 to April 1999, oil could break down into sludge and block oil passages, especially with longer oil change intervals. Toyota set up a special policy (TC02002) covering sludge damage for 8 years from purchase.
issues.next: That coverage has ended, so keep oil changes short (3,000-5,000 miles). If you see sludge under the oil filler cap, have the engine cleaned out before it starves for oil.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pump and front seals
issues.sym: Oil dripping from the front of the engine, behind the timing belt cover, and spots under the car.
issues.why: The oil pump O-ring and shaft seal and the crankshaft and camshaft seals harden and crack with age. Because they hold pressurized oil, even a small crack leaks heavily, and oil on the timing belt shortens its life.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Since the timing belt drives the oil pump, do the seals and timing belt together to save labor.

issues.t: Ignition coil inside the distributor fails
issues.sym: Hesitation, misfiring, stalling, or the engine cranking but not starting, often once warm.
issues.why: These Celicas have the ignition coil built into the distributor. Heat and age break the coil down. RepairPal has dozens of reports, averaging about 159,000 miles.
issues.next: Have spark tested when the problem happens. Replace the coil (or the whole distributor if the cap, rotor and seals are also worn).

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifting poorly at high mileage
issues.sym: Late, harsh or erratic shifts, or the transmission holding gears too long, usually past 140,000 miles.
issues.why: RepairPal links this to a failing throttle position sensor, which tells the transmission how hard you are pressing the gas. Worn fluid and internal wear also play a part.
issues.next: Have the throttle position sensor tested and the fluid checked before anyone recommends a rebuild.

issues.t: Power steering pump and hose leaks
issues.sym: Reddish fluid under the front of the car, a whine when turning, or heavier steering when the fluid gets low.
issues.why: The power steering pump seals and the pressure and return hoses wear and start to leak with age.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for wet hoses. Replace the leaking hose or pump before the pump runs dry and fails.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning beforehand. In a crash, the driver airbag may burst and throw metal pieces, or not inflate fully.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator can absorb moisture because of a manufacturing issue, which can make it rupture or underinflate. Toyota recall 20V-033 inspects the steering wheel airbag and replaces the inflator as needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls now and book the free repair right away if it is open.

issues.t: Add-on cruise control throttle linkage may stick (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may not return to idle when you lift off the gas, causing unintended acceleration.
issues.why: A Rostra cruise control kit fitted to some 1996 Celicas had a throttle linkage problem. Recall 96E-001 covered the kit.
issues.next: If your car has an add-on cruise control, check with a Toyota dealer that the recall repair was done. If the throttle ever sticks, shift to neutral and stop safely.

issues.t: Convertible top wearing where it rubs
issues.sym: Worn, shiny or torn spots on the soft top fabric where it folds or touches the frame, which can later let water in.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin 97062701897 covers complaints of the convertible top cover chafing and gives a repair procedure.
issues.next: Have the top's fit and contact points checked. Patch or replace worn areas before they tear and leak.

issues.t: Musty smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A sour or musty smell when the A/C or fan first comes on.
issues.why: Moisture on the A/C evaporator lets mold and bacteria grow. Toyota issued bulletin 97050900297 for excessive evaporator odor.
issues.next: Replace the cabin filter if fitted, run the fan with the A/C off for a few minutes before parking, and have the evaporator cleaned if the smell stays.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor code (P0335) from a weak battery
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0335, often with slow or hard starting in cold weather.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-TT-0010-10 says low battery voltage during cranking can set this code even when the sensor is fine.
issues.next: Test the battery and charging system before paying for a crank sensor.

issues.t: Manual transmission bearing whine and failure
issues.sym: A low grinding hum like a bad wheel bearing plus a whine in first through third gear that gets louder over a few thousand miles. It may pop out of gear before the transmission fails.
issues.why: The input shaft bearing in the GT's 5-speed manual wears out early. Owners report failures from about 36,000 to 105,000 miles.
issues.next: Have it checked as soon as the noise starts. Replacing the bearing early costs far less than a whole transmission after it lets go.

issues.t: Clutch wearing out early
issues.sym: The engine revs rise without the car speeding up, the pedal engages high, or there's a burning smell on hills.
issues.why: Owners report clutches worn out by about 56,000 miles. Spirited driving, common in these cars, speeds up wear.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked before it slips badly. Ask the shop to check the flywheel at the same time.

issues.t: Transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping between gears, revs flaring, or the transmission quitting, reported around 70,000-75,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of 2003-2004 Celicas report transmission slipping and failure. Low or worn fluid and internal wear are the usual causes.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have it diagnosed quickly, since driving a slipping transmission makes the damage worse.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fluid leak
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the middle of the car and the transmission fluid level drops.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin TC00300 covers an automatic transmission leak on early 2000 Celicas.
issues.next: Keep the fluid topped up and have the leak located; ask a dealer about the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Check engine light for variable valve timing (P1349)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P1349. The engine may idle rough or feel weak.
issues.why: Variable valve timing is driven by oil pressure. A sticking oil control valve or dirty oil can set this code. Toyota issued bulletin 00903 for it.
issues.next: Check the oil level and condition, then have the oil control valve and its screen tested.

issues.t: Check engine light and rough running in freezing weather
issues.sym: Rough running or stumbling when it's very cold, with a check engine light for lean (P0171), misfire (P030x) or oxygen sensor (P0133) codes.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin 04607 says the engine can run lean in subfreezing temperatures and set these codes, and gives a repair.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin. Check for vacuum leaks and a dirty airflow sensor too.

issues.t: Check engine light for misfire codes
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with random (P0300) or single-cylinder misfire codes, with rough running.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin 03104 covers misfire codes on these cars. Worn plugs or a failing coil can also cause it.
issues.next: Have the codes read and plugs and coils checked, and ask a dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Hard starting or rough idle after the battery is disconnected
issues.sym: After a battery change or jump, the car is hard to start or idles low and rough.
issues.why: The engine computer loses its learned idle settings when power is cut. Toyota bulletins T-TT-0362-15 and T-TT-0086-11 describe the relearn process.
issues.next: Let the engine idle for several minutes with accessories off, then drive normally. If it doesn't settle, a shop can run the idle relearn and clean the throttle body.

issues.t: Squeal or rattle when slowing down after a cold start
issues.sym: A squeal or rattle from the engine while coasting slowly, mainly after the car has sat overnight.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin EG01401 covers this noise on the 1.8L engines after a cold soak and gives dealers a fix.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to check the bulletin and the drive belt and tensioner.

issues.t: Rear hatch won't stay up
issues.sym: The rear hatch drifts down or drops shut on its own.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold up the hatch lose pressure. Toyota bulletin BO01502 addresses hatch stays that don't give enough support.
issues.next: Replace both struts as a pair. Until then, prop the hatch so it can't fall on anyone.

issues.t: Water leaking into the interior
issues.sym: Wet carpet, water drips inside, fogged windows or a musty smell.
issues.why: Seals around the doors, glass, hatch or moon roof drains wear or clog. Toyota bulletin T-SB-0094-21 covers finding water entry and removing musty odors.
issues.next: Have a water test done to find the leak, fix the seal or drain, and dry the carpet fully.

issues.t: Creak or tick from the windshield or rear glass
issues.sym: A creak, tick or rattle at the top or bottom of the windshield or the top of the rear glass, often over bumps.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-SB-0141-10 traces this to the glass's bonded stoppers or the glass moving slightly in its mounting.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or glass shop to follow the bulletin. It is a comfort issue, not a safety risk.

issues.t: Creaking moon roof
issues.sym: Creaks from the moon roof area over bumps or when the body flexes.
issues.why: Toyota bulletins NV00801 and 661 cover a moon roof creaking noise and how to fix it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to apply the bulletin fix; cleaning and lubricating the roof seals sometimes helps.

issues.t: Loose outer door handle
issues.sym: The outside door handle feels loose or wiggles, with a gap against the door.
issues.why: Toyota bulletins BO02300 and 288 describe a gap between the handle and door panel and how to reduce handle movement.
issues.next: A shop can adjust or shim the handle. Fix it before the linkage wears and the door becomes hard to open.

issues.t: Fuel can spill at the pump from a loose check valve (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel spurts out of the filler when the pump nozzle clicks off, with a strong gas smell.
issues.why: A check valve in the fuel filler pipe can separate and drop into the tank, so fuel can spill during refueling and create a fire risk. Toyota recall 03V-074 inspects and repairs the valve.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If fuel spills while filling, stop, clean it up away from ignition sources and have the recall done.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder seal can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid level dropping, fluid wetness at the master cylinder, or a soft or sinking pedal.
issues.why: A rubber seal ring in the master cylinder could corrode because of an improper washing process at the factory, letting fluid leak or air in and lengthening stops. Recall 04V-455 inspects and replaces the master cylinder and booster as needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the brakes checked if the pedal feels soft.

issues.t: Daytime running lights too bright (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom for the driver; the daytime running lights are brighter than federal rules allow.
issues.why: The daytime running lamps did not meet federal lighting standard 108. Recall 04V-566 adds a resistor to dim them.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether the free fix was done on your car.
